messages:
Elena (CFO): Quick follow-up from the all-hands re: runway and procurement controls. Posting the summary + a couple of concrete Qs we need answers to.
Jon (CEO): thanks Elena — can you call out any near-term risks that would materially change the runway number?
Elena (CFO): Not today. Our forecast still shows ~21-23 months under base case. Biggest sensitivity is 1) spike in Dedicated capacity use, 2) a few large professional services contracts landing in Q3.
Aisha (Head of Ops): For the PS contracts, are we asking for PO holds until legal/finance signoff?
Elena (CFO): Yes. New rule: no PS/consulting engagement > $25k can start without Finance + Legal countersign. We're also tightening card spend and vendor onboarding.
Maya (Procurement): Adding the updated approval matrix here for clarity:
```
<= $2k -> Employee + Manager
$2k - $25k -> Manager + Finance Ops (Luca)
$25k - $100k -> Director + Finance + Legal
> $100k -> VP + CFO + Legal
Emergency procured services (security incident/op outage) -> rapid approval channel + post-facto audit
```
Sam (SWE): Where does the commit for Dedicated capacity reservations live? Eng infra usually signs off but cost centers vary.
Luca (Finance Ops): Good Q. For Dedicated/GPU reservations we require cost center tag + email approval from owner. If the reservation is > $10k/mo, it follows the $25k threshold process (we pro-rate monthly). Put requests in the procurement queue and cc finance@redwood.com.
Aisha (Head of Ops): Who is the emergency approver chain? We need something workable after hours.
Elena (CFO): Emergency chain: on-call Eng lead -> Eng SRE lead -> Finance Ops on-call -> CFO. If any step is unreachable, the next person can approve with post-hoc review. We'll add a ticket template for emergency spend.
Sam (SWE): Can we get a short playbook for infra people — ideally a single doc that says "how to reserve GPUs", who to email, and what fields to include?
Maya (Procurement): I'll publish a checklist in Notion by EOD. Draft link: https://notion.redwood/inventory/procurement-playbook (will update permissions).
devops-bot: Reminder: purchase-policy.yml was changed in git by @Maya at 1829345950 — see changelog.
Luca (Finance Ops): A couple of concrete asks for teams: 1) tag cost centers on all infra requests 2) attach expected duration for capacity reservations 3) route any vendor onboarding to procurement before any invoices are paid.
Elena (CFO): Two final notes: 1) SLA credits — if a vendor misses an SLA and offers a credit, Finance will treat it as an offset against future invoices; push vendor to provide written credit terms. 2) Card limits — we'll reduce default card limit for ICs to $2k; exceptions via manager + Finance.
Jon (CEO): Sounds reasonable. Let's make these changes visible in the all-hands notes and the wiki. Good work.
Sam (SWE): :thumbsup: quick Q — will Dedicated autoscale bursts require extra approvals?
Maya (Procurement): Bursts that trigger >$5k incremental spend/month need a flagged review; if it's expected behavior of an app (spike), then Eng lead + Finance signoff. We'll add monitoring alerts so Finance gets notified.
Elena (CFO): OK — next steps: Maya publishes the procurement checklist and policy doc, Luca will add tagging requirements and an example PR template, Aisha will coordinate communication to managers. If anyone has blockers for their teams, ping me directly.
Jon (CEO): Thanks — please @channel when docs are live.
Sam (SWE): noted, will review checklist once posted.
Luca (Finance Ops): Posting the short FAQ tomorrow morning with examples (reserved GPU request, PS contract example).
Elena (CFO): closing the thread — appreciate the quick turnaround. :rocket:
